rationale.conceptual: The paper uses an established DFT method (LDA, plane waves, Troullier-Martins pseudopotentials) but the task demands accurate construction of two specific interface registries (strain-free and strained coherent) and careful total-energy scans. It requires understanding of periodic supercell geometry and pseudopotential selection, not a novel algorithm, but not trivial either.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves building atomic models for two registries, setting up a series of 322 DFT single-point calculations (161 distances per registry) with ABINIT, collecting total energies, computing relative energies, and outputting a CSV. This is a multi-step, moderately complex orchestration with dependency on proper ABINIT configuration and potential convergence issues.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires setting up DFT calculations for two specific interfacial models using ABINIT with LDA pseudopotentials, scanning interlayer distances to obtain potential energy curves. While the method (DFT) is standard, correctly constructing the supercell registries and running 322 total-energy calculations is non-trivial.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Plane-wave DFT on small supercells (few atoms) with norm-conserving pseudopotentials runs on CPU; 322 jobs each require minutes, total wall-time ~20-30 hours on a modern multi-core node. Memory per run ~2-4 GB, peak ~8 GB for the full series. Input geometry files are tiny.
